core.title: Give every authored document a corpus-unique identifier
core.given: The authored documentation corpus: every authored document of the stack's documentation file kind beneath the documentation root — archived documents included, never-scanned generated trees excluded.
core.when: Any declared document identifier is shared by another authored document in the corpus — newly introduced (created, copied, moved, archived) or pre-existing and surfaced by validation.
core.then: Ensure no two authored documents in the corpus declare the same document identifier.
prefer: An archived document and its replacement get DIFFERENT identifiers: the replacement is marked current and declares the succession edge to the archived identifier; the archived one is marked superseded.
The archive shares the identifier space on purpose: choose identifiers for archived documents that cannot collide with current ones.
avoid: Re-using a current identifier for an archived document: the resolver cannot tell superseding from superseded, so the succession edge fails exactly where it is needed.
Deleting a document to fix a duplicate; preserving history is the point.
Copying a template document without changing its identifier.
unless: Generated output in the never-scanned generated trees is outside the corpus and is never compared.
Documents that declare no identifier at all belong to the companion rule that requires identifiers; only declared identifiers are compared.
core.why: Uniqueness makes the document identifier an identity, not a label, so every reference edge resolves to exactly one target; a duplicate leaves a succession edge unable to say which of the two documents it means.
evidence: The corpus validation reports no duplicate document identifier across every authored document in the corpus (archived documents included, never-scanned generated trees excluded).
For any archived/replacement pair, the two documents carry distinct identifiers and the replacement declares the succession edge pointing at the archived identifier; neither document was deleted.
verification: Scope: every authored document in the corpus — the documentation root, all areas, archived documents included — excluding the never-scanned generated trees. Uniqueness is global: the archive is NOT a separate identifier space. Checked over the whole corpus, not only touched files.
Report EVERY document carrying a duplicated identifier, not just the second one: there is no principled basis for calling one of them the original.
Only compare identifiers that were actually declared; documents with no identifier are skipped here and belong to the companion rule that requires identifiers.
Severity 2; disposition strict: the checker fails on every finding of this rule — no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.

values: duplicate document identifier reported by the corpus validation

fires: The planner authors a new document in the corpus whose identifier equals one already declared elsewhere in the corpus.
The planner archives a document and writes its replacement with the same identifier as the archived copy in the archive.
The planner copies an existing document as a template and keeps its identifier unchanged.
A corpus validation (or a body-only edit or move of an unrelated document) surfaces two existing documents that already share an identifier, even though neither identifier was changed in this task.
doesNotFire: Generated output in a never-scanned generated tree shares an identifier with an authored document.
An authored document in the corpus declares no identifier at all (that is the companion rule requiring identifiers).
Edits to a document's body when every identifier in the corpus is unique.

profileRequirements.meaning: Root of the authored documentation corpus: every authored document beneath it, across all areas, belongs to the corpus.
The file suffix of authored documents; only documents of this kind declare identifiers.
Where archived documents live inside the documentation corpus; the archive is part of the corpus and shares its identifier space.
The one stack-wide list of vendored/generated trees that are never scanned; generated output inside the documentation root is outside the corpus through this list.
The syntax by which an authored document declares its own document identifier.
How the stack marks a document current vs superseded, and the construct by which a replacement declares succession of the archived document.

proposedKeys.meaning: Root of the authored documentation corpus that documentation rules scan.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The roots group covers config, source, test, e2e, plan and scan trees only; the authored documentation tree has no root key (roots.plan is plan artifacts, not docs).

proposedKeys.meaning: Where archived documents live inside the documentation corpus; the archive shares the corpus identifier space.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: Layout keys cover wagon/feature/code/plan/test/e2e placement only; there is no key for an archive location inside the documentation tree.

proposedKeys.meaning: The syntax by which an authored document declares its own document identifier.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: urn.declaration covers plan artifacts only and the urn.<artifact>/urn.binding.<artifact> params have no document kind; the doc-id attribute needs its own declaration key.

proposedKeys.meaning: How the stack marks a document current vs superseded, and the construct by which a replacement declares succession of the archived document.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: Existing idiom keys cover boundary/auth/error/validation/import/nesting/request-gate constructs; none describes document lifecycle or succession marking.

Reviewer fix example (from source): give the archived document a distinct id and link the succession explicitly:
  docs/architecture/shared-control-root.adoc
    :doc-id: architecture.shared-control-root
    :status: current
    :supersedes: archive.2025-control-root

  docs/archive/2025-control-root.adoc
    :doc-id: archive.2025-control-root
    :status: superseded

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself (corpus-wide identifier uniqueness, archive included, generated output excluded, only declared identifiers compared) is fully stack-neutral. Everything concrete is profile-supplied: documentation root, document suffix, archive location, generated-tree exclusion, identifier declaration syntax, and the current/superseded/succession constructs — the last four have no existing vocabulary keys and are proposed. Detector/validator ids (docs_capability), the companion rule id (planner.docs.identity-required) and the concrete reviewer fix example remain Bun-only; the core's verification describes the check generically. The 'planner' persona is kept as neutral workflow vocabulary (it names who authors docs, not a stack artifact). Severity and strict disposition stay in core:verification per the notProfileKeys list.
